channel.title: Acme: Daily Reading List
channel.description: Noteworthy articles from across the web.

item.title: A veterinarian's practical guide to safer floors for older dogs
item.description: Veterinarian Monica Tarantino recommends starting with washable non-skid runners in the few places an older dog hesitates or slips. She also suggests secured mats at food and water, trimmed nails and paw hair, stable ramps, nightlights and a two-week log of changes to discuss with a veterinarian.

item.title: Why the dots and misregistration made old comic books beautiful
item.description: The American Printing History Association revisits Gabriella Miyares's close study of four-color rotary letterpress comics. Coarse CMYK halftone screens, cheap newsprint and imperfect plate registration created the distinctive 1940s-to-1970s look that artists still imitate.

item.title: Catherine Asaro explains how physics and feminism shape her fiction
item.description: In a Daily Bruin profile, Catherine Asaro describes turning theoretical physics into the foundation of her Skolian Empire stories and using powerful female protagonists to challenge the science fiction she grew up reading. She also recalls plotting novels while teaching physics.

item.title: How Paul Bacon found the unforgettable image for Catch-22
item.description: Designer Paul Bacon made 11 versions of the Catch-22 jacket before landing on its fleeing red figure and handmade lettering. This compact retrospective explains the origin of his influential 'Big Book Look' across a career that produced roughly 6,500 book jackets.

item.title: Florida State's road drought reaches 14 straight losses
item.description: An Associated Press account of Florida State's double-overtime loss at Miami notes the Seminoles have lost 14 consecutive games away from Tallahassee. FSU is also 0-13 in true road games against ranked teams since its 2016 win at Miami.

item.title: Yelp explains why 'unique visitors' do not equal unique people
item.description: Yelp's 2025 annual report details the measurement caveats behind web-audience figures: one person on several devices can be counted several times, while several people sharing one device can count once. It also explains a 2025 methodology change that excludes home-page visits with no further action.

item.title: Reddit now documents community-specific karma gates
item.description: Reddit's Poster Eligibility Guide confirms that communities can require comment karma earned within that community, along with account age, total karma and verified email. It also explains that exact thresholds remain hidden and that Automoderator rules set to remove can block posting before submission.

item.title: Java 27 arrives with a fresh six-month feature release
item.description: Oracle's Java 27 overview introduces the September feature release and its language, runtime, security and library changes. It is a useful orientation for developers moving beyond Java 26, with links to the release notes and the OpenJDK work behind the new version.

item.title: Library of Congress opens a cabinet of archival specters
item.description: Library specialists tour spirit photography, the Bell Witch, gargoyles and horror comics preserved in the national collections. The comic-book section follows a crime title's transformation into horror while the wider piece shows how catalog records and archival context can unravel supposedly supernatural artifacts.

item.title: Copyright Office guide explains the old notice trap
item.description: Circular 3 is a compact guide to U.S. copyright notice rules. Notice became optional for works first published on or after March 1, 1989, but omission from older publications could forfeit protection unless statutory cure provisions or later restoration applied. Useful groundwork for copyright archaeology.

item.title: Stanford guide maps the clues that a work is in the public domain
item.description: Rich Stim's practical guide explains how to recognize public-domain works, including expired copyrights, U.S. government works and explicit dedication. It also warns that a missing notice alone proves little for newer publications and that only the copyright owner can dedicate a work.
item.source: Stanford Copyright and Fair Use Center

item.title: A 1996 WinSite CD preserves the shareware web before app stores
item.description: This browsable mirror preserves InfoMagic's WinSite archive as it stood on March 25, 1996. Its directory pages, descriptions and try-before-you-buy explanation capture the practical culture of Windows shareware distribution, including the expectation that satisfied users would pay authors.

item.title: FANAC restores a 1963 SFPA mailing with nine complete fanzines
item.description: The newly updated index for Southern Fandom Press Alliance mailing 10 opens 124 scanned pages from December 1963. The nine contributions include work by Rick Norwood, Dave Hulan, Bill Plott and Larry Montgomery, making an early slice of Southern fan publishing directly browsable.

item.title: St. Augustine’s oldest house reveals layers of Florida history
item.description: A News4JAX visit to the Ximenez-Fatio House and St. Augustine Historical Society traces more than 450 years of the city’s past, from Pedro Menéndez and Spanish rule through British occupation, territorial Florida and statehood.

item.title: Composable Script Includes can make ServiceNow code smaller and faster
item.description: Andy Halstead shows how ServiceNow’s server-side JavaScript libraries can be organized as small, composable functions. The approach reduces repeated class setup, encourages explicit dependencies and offers a practical route to reusable code in a constrained runtime.
